title: How to report an issue properly
summary: A quick checklist for writing a report that gets actioned faster.
body: Before you submit, check you've included: the exact building and room/area (not just "the library", but which floor or room), what's actually wrong rather than what you think caused it, and roughly when you first noticed it. Reports with a specific location get triaged first because the maintenance team don't have to chase you for details.

title: Choosing the right category
summary: What each category actually covers, so reports land with the right team.
body: Plumbing covers leaks, blockages and taps/toilets. Electrical covers sockets, lighting and anything that sparks, smells burnt, or trips. Heating/Cooling covers radiators, AC units and thermostats. Accessibility covers ramps, automatic doors, lifts and anything that stops someone getting around campus safely. If you're not sure, pick the closest one - reports can be recategorised by staff.

title: When to skip the form and call Estates directly
summary: Some things shouldn't wait for a queued report.
body: If there's a gas smell, exposed wiring, a flood, or anything that could hurt someone in the next hour, don't wait for this form to be reviewed - use the Estates emergency line on campus and report it here afterwards for the record.
